section has a **Lab task** for the lab computer and one set of questions.

## Key terms

{{< glossary account authentication single-sign-on file folder file-path file-extension file-size cloud-storage synchronization backup >}}

## 2.1 Your account and single sign-on

- An **account**: your user name, your password and your data.
- **Authentication**: you prove that the account is yours. Three kinds of
  proof: something you **know** (a password), **have** (your phone),
  **are** (your fingerprint).
- **Single sign-on (SSO)**: you sign in one time, and all university services open.
- Risk: a stolen password opens everything.
- On a lab computer: sign out, never save your password, lock the screen
  (Windows key + L).

![Single sign-on.](images/sso.png){width=84%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Closing the browser does not always sign you out. Press **Sign out** first.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · One sign-in, many services"}
Sign in to your university account. Open the e-mail, the e-learning platform
and the cloud storage. How many times did you type your password? At the end,
sign out and lock the screen.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Accounts and sign-in"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="something you are"}
A code comes to your phone. Which kind of proof is it?
:   something you have

Your password. Which kind of proof is it?
:   something you know

You sign in one time, and e-mail and e-learning both open. What is this called?
:   single sign-on

What is the risk of single sign-on?
:   a stolen password opens everything

You leave your lab desk for one minute. What do you do?
:   lock the screen
:::
:::

## 2.2 Files, folders and paths

- A **file**: one saved piece of work (a document, a photo, a video).
- A **folder** keeps files and other folders. Folders in folders make a tree.
- The **path** is the full address of a file. Example on Windows:
  `C:\Users\Sara\Documents\Courses\Digital-Skills\week-01\cv.docx`
- Two files can have the same name, but never the same path.
- The **extension** (`.docx`, `.jpg`, `.exe`) shows the type of the file.
- **File size:** each unit is 1024 times the one before.
  1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB. Example: 2 GB = 2048 MB.
- A document is a few KB, a photo a few MB, a video often hundreds of MB.

![A folder tree.](images/folder-tree.png){width=86%}

{{< sim file="sims/path-finder.html" poster="sims/path-finder.png" title="Path Finder: files, folders and paths" kind="game" height="600" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
`invoice.pdf.exe` looks like `invoice.pdf` when Windows hides extensions. Turn
on **File name extensions**.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Extensions, sizes and paths"}
In File Explorer, turn on **File name extensions**. Write the extension and
the size of three files. Right-click one file → **Copy as path**, and paste
it into a document. Then play stage 1 of **Path Finder**.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Paths, types and sizes"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Word|3000 MB"}
Two files are both called `cv.docx`. What is always different?
:   their paths

Which app opens `budget.xlsx`?
:   Excel

A file is called `photo.jpg.exe`. What is it really?
:   a program

A document, a photo and a video. Which is usually the biggest?
:   the video

A video is 3 GB. How many MB is it?
:   3072 MB
:::
:::

## 2.3 Good file names and folders

- Say what it is: `cv`, not `New Document`.
- No spaces: use `-` or `_`.
- Dates as year-month-day: 2026-10-21. Then the files sort by date.
- Versions: `v01`, `v02`, not `final2`.
- One folder for each course, one folder for each week. Four levels or fewer.

| Poor name | Better name |
|---|---|
| `New Document (3).docx` | `2026-10-21_cv_v01.docx` |
| `final final.pptx` | `2026-11-12_english-talk_v03.pptx` |
| `IMG_4821.jpg` | `2026-10-21_family-dinner.jpg` |

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Make your course folders"}
In your cloud storage, make `Courses`, one folder for each course, and
`Digital-Skills/week-01`. Put your DigComp profile in `week-01` and give it a
good name, for example `2026-10-21_digcomp-profile_v01.pdf`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Good names"}
Choose the better answer.

::: {.match extra="21-10-2026|final_v2_new"}
A better name for `final final.pptx` (an English talk, 12 November 2026, third version).
:   2026-11-12_english-talk_v03.pptx

Which date format sorts files by date?
:   2026-10-21

What do you use instead of spaces in a file name?
:   - or _

How do you mark the second version of a file?
:   v02
:::
:::

## 2.4 Cloud storage, sync and backup

- **Cloud storage**: your files on the Internet; open them on any device.
- **Sync**: the same files on all your devices. It also copies your mistakes.
- **Backup**: an extra copy in a separate place. A mistake does not reach it.
- The recycle bin and the version history help for some days.
- **3-2-1 rule**: 3 copies, 2 kinds of storage, 1 copy in another place.

![Sync and backup.](images/sync-backup.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Delete and get it back"}
Rename your file to `v02`. Delete it. Restore it from the **recycle bin** of
the cloud storage. How many days does your recycle bin keep files?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Sync or backup?"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="sync is a backup|2 copies"}
You delete a file on the lab computer. What happens on your synced phone?
:   it is deleted too

A copy of your work on a USB stick at home. What is it?
:   a backup

Where can you find a deleted file for some days?
:   the recycle bin

The 3-2-1 rule: how many copies?
:   3 copies
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Sara's class report {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Sara writes a class report on the lab computer (Windows, user `Sara`). Her
folder is `Documents\Courses\English\week-01`. In it are a photo
`photo.jpg` and a document `final final (2).docx`, made on 5 November 2026.
The folder is synced with her cloud storage. Every Sunday she copies it to a
USB stick at home.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Sara's report (harder)"}
Sara (Windows, user `Sara`): `Documents\Courses\English\week-01` has
`photo.jpg` and `final final (2).docx` (5 November 2026). The folder is
synced. A USB copy is at home. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="final_v3.docx|her synced laptop"}
A better name for `final final (2).docx`.
:   2026-11-05_report_v01.docx

Which app opens `photo.jpg`?
:   a photo app

The path of `photo.jpg`.
:   C:\\Users\\Sara\\Documents\\Courses\\English\\week-01\\photo.jpg

She deletes the folder on the lab computer by mistake. Where can she get it back first?
:   the cloud recycle bin

What is her USB copy at home in the 3-2-1 rule?
:   the copy in another place
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- You prove an account is yours with something you know, have or are.
- Single sign-on: one sign-in opens many services.
- A path is the full address of a file in the folder tree.
- Show extensions; each size unit is 1024 times the one before.
- Good names: date (year-month-day), what it is, version (v01).
- Sync copies your mistakes; a backup does not.
